newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares close down, A shares end higher.
newsitem.headline: China B shares close down, A shares end higher.

text.p: China's hard currency B shares closed down on Friday as investors retreated from the market to wait for interim results or buy Hong Kong stocks, brokers said.
Domestic currency A shares gained but remained locked in the current trading range in both Shanghai and Shenzhen, they said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended slightly down in thin trade, with many investors retreating from the market amid weak sentiment, brokers said.

Recent rises in the Hong Kong stock market had drained foreign funds from B shares and domestic investors were cautious in the lead up to 1997 interim reports, due to be released by the end of August, they said.
The Shanghai B index edged down 0.079 points or 0.10 percent to 76.369 points on volume of 9.434 million shares worth $5.459 million.
"Major institutions have left the market and investor sentiment won't revive in the short term," a local broker said.
Selling of electric appliance-related stocks late in the afternoon session depressed the market, but trading was still sluggish with little investor interest, brokers said.
Of 45 B shares, 36 traded with 14 down, 13 up and nine flat.
Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliances Co was the biggest loser on talk of poor interim results. It plunged 9.8 percent or $0.020 to $0.184.
Shanghai's A shares ended up on light speculative buying, but sentiment was cautious amid market uncertainties, brokers said.
The Shanghai A index rose 13.599 points or 1.09 percent to 1,265.613 points on volume of 459.386 million shares worth 5.937 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index gained 30.113 points or 0.78 percent to 3,904.582 points.
Shenzhen's hard currency B shares ended a quiet day slightly lower, with many foreign investors diverting funds to Hong Kong-listed H shares, analysts said.
H shares are offered by mainland Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong.
The Shenzhen B share index closed at 133.17 points, down 0.47 or 0.35 percent. B share turnover was HK$46 million, little changed from Thursday.
"The B share trading volume has been really light because many people are diverting funds to the more exciting H share market," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
Beijing's crackdown in May on stock-related irregularities had dampened speculation, leading to lower turnover, analysts said.
The Chinese yuan-based A share index gained 4.51 points or 1.09 percent to 419.64 points on turnover of 7.7 billion yuan against Thursday's 6.8 billion yuan.
In the B share market, television tube maker Shijiazhuang Baoshi Electronic Co Ltd was the worst performer, sagging HK$0.10 or 4.50 percent to HK$2.12.
